subject: Questions about uptime/latency measurement, alerts, and customer metrics access
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@finbank.com>

Cc: procurement@finbank.com

Subject: Procurement questionnaire — uptime/latency measurement and customer access

Hi Rishi,

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement at FinBank has one follow-up packet focused on how you measure and present uptime and latency SLOs. We're trying to standardize supplier responses. Below are the items they asked for — can you confirm and provide any attachments we can ship to our procurement reviewers?

1) Precise SLO definitions you commit to for hosted accounts (example: 99.95% availability, 99th percentile p99 latency <= 250ms for text generation tokens). Please include the measurement window (monthly/rolling 30d) and what counts as a successful request.

2) What monitoring platform collects the telemetry? Do you expose our account-level metrics (latency percentiles, error rates) in a dashboard we can access? If so, how (role-based dashboard link, API)?

3) Incident/exclusion policy: how do you treat scheduled maintenance, customer-induced outages, or upstream cloud provider incidents in the SLO calculation?

4) Alerting — what thresholds trigger alerts to customers and to Redwood on-call? Please include escalation paths and expected initial response times.

5) Retention: how long do you retain raw traces, request logs, and aggregated SLO time series? Can we request historical exports?

6) Exceptions & credits: if you miss the SLO, what's the process to request exception/credit? Is there a formal form or can we raise a case? Timeline to resolution?

7) Any sample export (CSV/JSON) of the per-account SLO time series and a sample of the dashboard invite flow would be helpful.

We'd like a consolidated response we can attach to our Security/Procurement packet by EOD Wednesday (2026-11-03). Let me know if you need more time.

Best,
Elena
Procurement — FinBank

Subject: Re: Procurement questionnaire — uptime/latency measurement and customer access

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear list. I've drafted answers below and attached a small sample export. I also looped in Marissa from Solutions for the billing/SLA language and Karthik from SRE for any technical clarifications. If anything needs more detail we can produce a short appendix for procurement.

1) SLO definitions / measurement windows- For hosted accounts we offer a default availability SLO of 99.95% measured as the percentage of successful request attempts over a rolling 30-day window, and latency SLOs expressed as percentage of requests meeting per-token generation latency thresholds (we typically publish p50/p95/p99). Success is defined as a 2xx response and a token stream without service errors. These are configurable per contract.

2) Monitoring and account-level access- Telemetry is collected by our internal telemetry service and pushed to an observability stack (Prometheus/Thanos for timeseries + Grafana for dashboards). For customers we can provision a role-based read-only dashboard scoped to their account with per-route and per-model views; we also expose a REST export endpoint for programmatic pulls.

3) Incident/exclusion policy- Scheduled maintenance windows >30 minutes are excluded from SLO calculations if agreed in advance. Customer-caused outages (misconfiguration, API keys revoked) are excluded if we can attribute causality. Cloud-provider severe incidents follow our RCA process; exclusions are only granted after post-incident review and documented in the monthly SLO report.

4) Alerting- We send automated alerts for error-rate or latency regressions exceeding configured thresholds (default: error rate >0.5% sustained over 5 minutes; p99 latency >500ms sustained over 5 minutes). On-call is paged immediately for high-severity incidents (P1/P2) with initial ack target of 15 minutes. Customers can subscribe to email/webhook alerts or request PagerDuty integration under an enterprise plan.

5) Retention- Aggregated SLO time series retained for 13 months by default; raw request logs and traces retained for 90 days. We can provide exports for procurement within 3 business days for historical ranges within retention.

6) Exceptions & credits- Exceptions are handled via a formal request (SLO Exception Request form) submitted to support.redwood.ai which routes to the SRE & Contracts teams. Typical review timeline is 5 business days; credits are computed per contract terms and applied as invoice adjustments. For procurement, we can provide a copy of the exception request template.

7) Attachments- I've attached a sample CSV with a 30-day SLO time series and included a temporary dashboard invite link in a follow-up note.

If this looks good I'll consolidate into a single PDF for your packet.

Thanks,
Rishi
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference

Thanks for the ping. Quick technical confirmation and a couple of suggested clarifications for procurement copy:

- Thresholds/alerts: default error-rate threshold of 0.5% sustained for 5 minutes is correct for automated alerting; we can reduce to 0.2% for enterprise-tier contracts if requested. p99 latency thresholds depend on model and request size — we recommend quoting model-specific p99s in the contract rather than a single platform number.

- Retention: 90 days for raw traces, 13 months for aggregated SLO TS is the standard we operate to. We can provide longer aggregated retention as a paid add-on; for exports our ops team can produce bucketed CSVs within 3 business days.

- Exclusions: scheduled maintenance is excluded only if notified >72 hours in advance and posted in the customer's account calendar; urgent maintenance under 72 hours is excluded only after communications and a post-mortem review. Customer-caused outages require evidence (support ticket, misconfig details) to be excluded.

- Exception path: we have an SLO Exception Request process (form -> SRE review -> Contracts approval). Turnaround: target 5 business days; for priority enterprise customers we can do 48-72 hours.

I've attached the ops runbook excerpt that procurement sometimes wants to see (redacted). Also adding sample contract phrasing below you can use verbatim in the response PDF.

Suggested procurement wording (for inclusion):
"Redwood Inference measures availability as the percentage of successful HTTP request attempts over a rolling 30-day window. Scheduled maintenance events are excluded when notified at least 72 hours in advance and documented in the customer's account. Exceptions to SLO calculations are handled through Redwood's SLO Exception Request process; typical review time is 5 business days."

-Karthik

Subject: Consolidated procurement response — SLO measurement, alerts, and access

Hi Elena — thanks for the patience. Please find the consolidated answers below and attached documents for your packet. If procurement wants a single PDF we can produce one today.

Summary answers (full language and attachments enclosed):
- SLOs: Default availability target 99.95% (rolling 30d). Latency reported as percentiles (p50/p95/p99) per model; contract will specify model-specific p99 thresholds.
- Measurement: Internal telemetry aggregated into account-level time series; success = 2xx / no service error.
- Dashboards & exports: We will provision a read-only Grafana dashboard scoped to FinBank and provide a REST export endpoint; included a temporary invite link in the attachments.
- Exclusions: Scheduled maintenance excluded if notified >=72 hours; customer-caused events require documentation. Cloud provider incidents are evaluated case-by-case and documented in the monthly SLO report.
- Alerting: Default automated alerts for sustained error-rate/latency regressions; initial on-call ack target 15 minutes (enterprise options for PagerDuty).
- Retention: Raw traces 90 days, aggregated SLO time series 13 months; exports available on request within 3 business days.
- Exceptions & credits: Use the SLO Exception Request form (attached). Typical review 5 business days; expedited review for enterprise customers (48-72 hours). Credits handled per contract.

Attachments included: SLO-measurement-examples.csv, ops-runbook.pdf (redacted), and a plain-text temporary dashboard invite (customer-dashboard-invite-link.txt).

If you want, we can schedule a 30-minute call with Karthik and Marissa to walk procurement through the dashboard and the exception workflow.

Best regards,
Rishi Malhotra
